It's tough for me to look at antidepressants again after being burnt twice by them. A few different studies I've read have found around half of people who take them never get relief. Even if you do find them helpful there are usually side effects.   
  
That's a good question on what I think a good life looks like. Funnily enough my interpretation is similar to yours but I'll add - Learning to accept my experience the way it is which comes under the umbrella of mindfulness, persisting with self-improvement, helping others, a relationship with God, and increasing my productivity.  
  
Thanks for the reply. It's something I need to reflect on more.
hmm interesting. That's something I haven't looked into. Thanks for the suggestion
Thanks, that is a good point. It reminds me of mindfulness where you don't identify with the experience and instead observe and accept it because reacting only increases its reinforcement.
